mainTopic: The days for reading the מגילה, the scriptural source for the early village readings, and whether early reading applies nowadays
overview: The משנה opens מסכת מגילה by saying the מגילה may be read on any day from the 11th to the 15th of אדר. Walled cities from the time of יהושע בן נון read on the 15th, towns read on the 14th, and villages may read early on the nearest יום הכניסה (Monday or Thursday). The משנה then goes through each weekday on which the 14th can fall. The גמרא asks where the early days are hinted in the פסוק, since a later בית דין could not have added them to the rule of אנשי כנסת הגדולה. רב שמן בר אבא learns them from the plural ״בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם״, and רבי שמואל בר נחמני learns them from ״כַּיָּמִים״. Both reach the 11th and 12th: the 13th needs no source, and ״וְלֹא יַעֲבוֹר״ rules out later days. רבי יוחנן then says the משנה follows רבי עקיבא. His first version is refuted by a ברייתא of רבי יהודה, and a second version, which forbids early reading only nowadays, is supported by that same ברייתא. The amud ends as רב אשי begins to point out a contradiction between two rulings of רבי יהודה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The מגילה can be read from the 11th to the 15th
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens by listing the five possible dates for reading the מגילה and says no other day is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מגילה is read on the 11th, 12th, 13th, 14th, or 15th of אדר. Not earlier and not later.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the whole range of days on which the מגילה may ever be read. It will explain who reads on which day in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally פורים is the 14th or 15th, so it is surprising that the 11th, 12th, and 13th are listed too. The rest of the משנה explains how those early dates come up. 'Not earlier and not later' sets firm limits: nobody may ever read before the 11th or after the 15th.

keyTerms.meaning: Not less and not more – no earlier than the 11th, no later than the 15th

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not mean that anyone may pick any of these five days. Each type of place has its own specific day, as the next lines explain.

phrases.english: The Megillah is read on the eleventh,
on the twelfth, on the thirteenth,
on the fourteenth, on the fifteenth (of Adar).
Not earlier, and not later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening statement of the מסכת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The valid days for reading the מגילה are the 11th through the 15th of אדר only.

steps.title: Walled cities read on the 15th, towns on the 14th, villages may read early
steps.stepSummary: The משנה assigns the basic days: walled cities on the 15th, villages and large towns on the 14th. Villages are allowed to read earlier, on the day of assembly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Cities that have had a wall around them since the days of יהושע בן נון read on the 15th. Villages and large towns read on the 14th. But the villages may move their reading earlier, to the day of assembly.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets out the three types of places and the basic reading day for each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dividing line is a wall that existed back in the time of יהושע בן נון, not a wall that exists today. Large towns and villages both belong to the 14th. However, villages get a special leniency: they may read earlier, on the יום הכניסה (a Monday or Thursday). On those days the villagers came into town for the courts and the קריאת התורה, so someone was available to read the מגילה for them.

keyTerms.meaning: Day of assembly – Monday or Thursday, when villagers came to town

steps.whyThisMatters: These three categories (כרכים, עיירות, כפרים) are the basis for every case that follows in the משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: The villages still belong to the 14th. Reading on יום הכניסה is an early version of the 14th, not a different holiday.

phrases.english: Cities that are surrounded by a wall
since the days of Joshua son of Nun —
read on the fifteenth;
villages and large towns —
read on the fourteenth;
except that the villages advance their reading to the day of assembly.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַכִּין הַמּוּקָּפִין חוֹמָה מִימוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which places use which of the dates listed in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Walled cities read on the 15th. Villages and large towns read on the 14th. Villages may move their reading earlier to יום הכניסה.

steps.title: When the 14th falls on Monday
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins its weekday-by-weekday breakdown. If the 14th is a Monday, villages and towns read that day and walled cities read the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this work? If the 14th falls on Monday, villages and large towns read on that day, and walled cities read the next day.
steps.whatsHappening: The word כיצד ('how so?') opens a detailed walkthrough of every possible weekday. This first case is Monday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Monday is itself a יום הכניסה. The villages therefore have no reason to read earlier, and they read on the 14th together with the towns. The walled cities read on Tuesday, the 15th, as usual.

keyTerms.meaning: It happened to fall (on that day)
On Monday (the second day of the week)

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיצַד: חָל לִהְיוֹת אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר בַּשֵּׁנִי —
phrases.english: How so? If the fourteenth fell on Monday —

phrases.aramaic: כְּפָרִים וַעֲיָירוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת קוֹרִין בּוֹ בַיּוֹם,
phrases.english: villages and large towns read on that day,
and walled cities on the next day.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד: חָל לִהְיוֹת אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר בַּשֵּׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins applying the rules of step 2 to specific weekdays
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 14th on Monday: villages and towns read Monday (14th); walled cities read Tuesday (15th).

steps.title: When the 14th falls on Tuesday or Wednesday
steps.stepSummary: The villages move back to Monday, the towns read on the 14th, and the walled cities read on the 15th.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the 14th falls on Tuesday or Wednesday, villages read earlier, on the day of assembly (Monday). Large towns read on that day (the 14th), and walled cities read the next day.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the case where the 14th is not a יום הכניסה. The villages therefore move back to the previous Monday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the 14th is Tuesday, the villages read on Monday the 13th. If it is Wednesday, they read on Monday the 12th. This is how the 13th and 12th from step 1 come into use.

phrases.english: If it fell on Tuesday or Wednesday —
villages advance to the day of assembly (Monday),
and large towns read on that day,
and walled cities on the next day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next weekday case in the series
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 14th on Tuesday or Wednesday: villages read on Monday (13th or 12th); towns on the 14th; walled cities on the 15th.

steps.title: When the 14th falls on Thursday
steps.stepSummary: Thursday is a day of assembly, so villages and towns read together on the 14th. Walled cities read on Friday.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the 14th falls on Thursday, villages and large towns read on that day, and walled cities read the next day.
steps.whatsHappening: This case works just like Monday, because Thursday is also a יום הכניסה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The villages do not need to move back, because the 14th is already a day of assembly. The walled cities read on Friday, the 15th, without any problem.

phrases.english: If it fell on Thursday —

phrases.aramaic: כְּפָרִים וַעֲיָירוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת קוֹרִין בּוֹ בַיּוֹם,
phrases.english: villages and large towns read on that day,
and walled cities on the next day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next weekday case, parallel to the Monday case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 14th on Thursday: villages and towns read Thursday (14th); walled cities read Friday (15th).

steps.title: When the 14th falls on Friday
steps.stepSummary: Villages read on Thursday. Towns and walled cities both read on Friday, the 14th.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the 14th falls on Friday (ערב שבת), villages read earlier, on the day of assembly (Thursday). Large towns and walled cities both read on that day (Friday).
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first case where the walled cities do not read on the 15th, because the 15th would be שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מגילה is not read on שבת. The walled cities therefore move back one day and join the towns on the 14th. The villages go back to Thursday, the 13th. This is an exception in how the walled cities' law is carried out; they remain walled cities.
steps.confusionAlert: Walled cities reading on the 14th here does not make them 'regular towns.' They read early only because the 15th is שבת.

phrases.english: If it fell on Friday —
villages advance to the day of assembly (Thursday),
and large towns and walled cities
read on that day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next weekday case; introduces the effect of שבת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 14th on Friday: villages read Thursday (13th); towns and walled cities read Friday (14th).

steps.title: When the 14th falls on שבת
steps.stepSummary: Villages and towns both move back to Thursday. Walled cities read on Sunday, the 15th.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the 14th falls on שבת, villages and large towns both read earlier, on the day of assembly (Thursday). Walled cities read the next day (Sunday).
steps.whatsHappening: Since the מגילה is not read on שבת, even the large towns must read early. They join the villages on the day of assembly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The towns and villages read on Thursday, the 12th. The walled cities are not affected by שבת, because their day is the 15th, which is Sunday. So they read on time.

phrases.english: If it fell on Shabbat —
villages and large towns
advance and read on the day of assembly (Thursday),
and walled cities on the next day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next weekday case; שבת now affects the towns
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 14th on שבת: villages and towns read Thursday (12th); walled cities read Sunday (15th).

steps.title: When the 14th falls on Sunday
steps.stepSummary: Villages go all the way back to Thursday the 11th. Towns read on Sunday and walled cities read on Monday.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the 14th falls on Sunday, villages read earlier, on the day of assembly (Thursday). Large towns read on that day (Sunday), and walled cities read the next day (Monday).
steps.whatsHappening: This last case finishes the weekday list and shows where the earliest date, the 11th, comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nearest earlier day of assembly before a Sunday is the Thursday before. That Thursday is the 11th. This is the earliest the מגילה is ever read, which explains the 'not earlier' limit in step 1.
steps.whatToRemember: Walled cities read on the 15th, and towns read on the 14th. Villages may read on the nearest earlier day of assembly (Monday or Thursday). Since the מגילה is not read on שבת, some readings move earlier. Across all the weekday cases, the reading days run from the 11th to the 15th.
steps.whyThisMatters: This case shows why the range in the משנה begins at the 11th. The גמרא will soon ask where these early days come from.

phrases.english: If it fell after Shabbat (Sunday) —
villages advance to the day of assembly (Thursday),
and large towns read on that day,
and walled cities on the next day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final weekday case; completes the explanation of the five dates from step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 14th on Sunday: villages read Thursday (11th); towns read Sunday (14th); walled cities read Monday (15th).

steps.title: Where do we learn that the מגילה can be read on the 11th?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of the משנה and asks for their source.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The מגילה is read on the 11th. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting the first line of the משנה, that the מגילה can be read on the 11th of אדר. It then asks where this rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מגילה itself only mentions the 14th and 15th of אדר. So reading on the 11th needs a source. This question opens the whole discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: The תלמוד's discussion of the משנה
The scroll of אסתר, read on פורים
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: Gemara:
The Megillah is read on the eleventh.
From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה's calendar cases to the source for the earliest reading day.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for reading the מגילה on the 11th of אדר.

steps.title: The question seems unnecessary because חכמים allowed it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised by the question. We already know the reason: חכמים let the כפרים read early so they could bring food to the cities.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why ask 'from where do we know'? As we will say later: חכמים were lenient with the villages and let them read early, on the day of assembly, so they could supply water and food to their brothers in the cities.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own question. It says the answer is already known: it is a leniency of חכמים for the כפרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes that reading on the 11th is simply a later rabbinic leniency. If so, there is no need to search for a source. The villagers read early on יום הכניסה (Monday or Thursday), when they come to town anyway, so they are free on Purim to help the people in the כרכים.

keyTerms.meaning: Day of assembly (Monday or Thursday, when villagers came to town)

phrases.english: From where do we know?! (Why ask?)
As we are going to say later on:
The Sages were lenient with the villages
to let them read early, on the day of assembly,
so that they can supply water and food
to their brothers in the cities.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the question of step 9 is needed at all.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reading on the 11th is a known rabbinic leniency for the villages, so no source is needed.

steps.title: The real question: all the days were set by אנשי כנסת הגדולה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains its question. It assumes all the reading days came from אנשי כנסת הגדולה, not from later חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what we meant: after all, אנשי כנסת הגדולה enacted all of these days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies what it was really asking. It starts from the idea that every reading day, including the 11th, was set up by אנשי כנסת הגדולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was never 'what is the reason for reading early?' It was 'where is the source in the פסוק?' This only makes sense if the early days are as old as פורים itself. The next step proves that idea.

keyTerms.meaning: The Men of the Great Assembly, who set up פורים

phrases.english: This is what we meant:
After all, all of them (all these days)
the Men of the Great Assembly enacted them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by restating the question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the intent of the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question asked for the reason behind the 11th, which is the known rabbinic leniency.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question asks for a scriptural hint, because all the days came from אנשי כנסת הגדולה.

steps.title: Proof: a later בית דין could not cancel the rule of אנשי כנסת הגדולה
steps.stepSummary: If אנשי כנסת הגדולה had set only the 14th and 15th, later חכמים could not have changed that. A בית דין cannot cancel another בית דין unless it is greater in wisdom and in number.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you thought אנשי כנסת הגדולה enacted only the 14th and 15th, would the later רבנן come and uproot their enactment? But we learned in a משנה: a בית דין cannot cancel the words of another בית דין unless it is greater than it in wisdom and in number.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that the early days must come from אנשי כנסת הגדולה. It cites a משנה that limits when a later בית דין may cancel an earlier ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Letting villages read on the 11th would cancel the original rule of the 14th and 15th for them. Only a greater בית דין could do that, and no court was ever greater than אנשי כנסת הגדולה. So the early days must have been part of their original enactment.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The later court must be greater in BOTH wisdom and number. Being greater in only one is not enough to cancel an earlier ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule about one בית דין cancelling another is a basic principle for how rabbinic enactments work across generations.

phrases.english: For if you would think
that the Men of the Great Assembly
enacted only the fourteenth and fifteenth,
would the Rabbis come and uproot
an enactment that the Men of the Great Assembly made?
But we learned in a Mishnah:
A court cannot cancel
the words of another court
unless it is greater than it
in wisdom and in number.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim made in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That all the reading days were enacted by אנשי כנסת הגדולה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in עדיות: a בית דין cannot cancel another בית דין unless greater in wisdom and number.

steps.title: So where is the extra-days rule hinted in the verse?
steps.stepSummary: Since it is clear that אנשי כנסת הגדולה set all the days, the גמרא asks where the פסוק hints at them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that אנשי כנסת הגדולה enacted all of them. Where is it hinted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up what was just proven and then asks its real question again: where is this hinted in the מגילה? It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מגילה, which אנשי כנסת הגדולה approved, mentions only the 14th and 15th. If they also set up earlier days, we expect some hint in the text. That hint is what the גמרא is looking for.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious
that the Men of the Great Assembly enacted all of them.
Where is it hinted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the proof of step 12 to restate the real question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A hint in the פסוק for the extra reading days.

steps.title: The word 'in their times' hints at many reading days
steps.stepSummary: רב שמן בר אבא quotes רבי יוחנן: the פסוק says ״בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם״, in the plural, teaching that many times were set up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמן בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The פסוק says, 'To establish these days of פורים in their times' (אסתר ט:לא). They enacted many times for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 13. רבי יוחנן finds the hint in the word ״בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם״ (in their times).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural word 'times' suggests more than the two basic days of the 14th and 15th. So אנשי כנסת הגדולה built several reading days into פורים from the start. This includes the early days for the כפרים.
steps.whatToRemember: The early reading days are not a later leniency. אנשי כנסת הגדולה set them up from the beginning, as hinted by the plural ״בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם״.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the base for the rest of the sugya, which will search for exactly which days are included in 'their times.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rav Shemen bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
The verse says:
"To establish these days of Purim
in their times"
phrases.notes: אסתר ט:לא. Notice the plural, "times": that's the key.

phrases.english: They enacted many times for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural ״בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם״ in אסתר ט:לא hints that many reading times were set up.

steps.title: The word is needed for its simple meaning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that ״בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם״ is needed to teach that פורים must be kept at its proper time, so it cannot also hint at extra days.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this word is needed for its own simple purpose!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's proof. It says the word ״בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם״ already has a basic job, so it is not free to teach extra days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple meaning of the פסוק is that the days of פורים must be kept on time. If the word is busy teaching that, we cannot use it to also teach that the כפרים may read early. The challenge targets the source, not the rule itself.

keyTerms.meaning: it is needed for it (this word already has a job)

phrases.english: This is needed for its own purpose!
phrases.notes: The basic meaning: keep the days of פורים at their proper time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivation that רבי יוחנן gave in step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's use of ״בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם״ as a source for extra reading days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A word that is needed for its plain meaning cannot also be used to teach a new law

steps.title: The plural form shows extra meaning
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק only meant 'on time', it would have said ״זְמַן״ (singular). The plural ״זְמַנֵּיהֶם״ teaches many times.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the פסוק should have said ״זְמַן״, 'time'. Why does it say ״זְמַנֵּיהֶם״, 'their times'? To teach that there are many times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The simple meaning only needs a singular word, so the plural form must be adding something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain lesson, 'keep פורים on time', could be taught with the singular ״זְמַן״. Since the פסוק uses a plural, that extra form is free to teach more: there are several times for reading.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say "time",
why "their times"?
Many times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording: the plural form is more than the simple meaning needs
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word is fully used up by its simple meaning
steps.terutzMaskana: The plural form is extra and teaches many times

steps.title: Maybe the plural only means different cities have different days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects again: the plural may only be teaching that walled cities and open towns read on different days.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, the plural is needed to teach that this place's time is not like that place's time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second job for the plural word. Maybe it only teaches that some places read on the 14th and others on the 15th.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walled cities read on the 15th and open towns read on the 14th. That already makes two different 'times', so the plural could be used up by this. If so, there is still no source for the early days.

keyTerms.meaning: the time of this one (this place)

phrases.english: But still, it is needed:
the time of this one
phrases.notes: For example, a walled city that reads on the 15th.

phrases.english: is not like the time of that one!
phrases.notes: For example, an open town that reads on the 14th.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another use for the plural form that step 16 relied on
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 16 that the plural teaches extra reading days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural is needed to show that the 14th and the 15th belong to different places, so nothing is left over

steps.title: A double plural teaches all the days
steps.stepSummary: For different cities, the simpler plural ״זְמַנָּם״ would be enough. The longer ״זְמַנֵּיהֶם״ teaches all the days listed in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the פסוק should have said ״זְמַנָּם״, 'their time'. Why does it say ״זְמַנֵּיהֶם״, 'their times'? Learn from it all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word ״זְמַנֵּיהֶם״ is a double plural. It is even more than 'different cities' needs, so it teaches all the days in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״זְמַנָּם״, 'their time', already covers each place with its own day. ״זְמַנֵּיהֶם″ adds a second plural ending. That extra layer teaches the early reading days for the כפרים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the proof that the early reading days are hinted at in the פסוק, as the גמרא assumed in steps 11 to 13.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say "their time",
why "their times"?
Learn from it all of them.
phrases.notes: All the days listed in the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording: a double plural beyond the simple plural
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural only shows that different places have different days
steps.terutzMaskana: ״זְמַנָּם״ would teach that, so ״זְמַנֵּיהֶם״ teaches all the days of the משנה

steps.title: Then maybe there are many more days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the plural teaches extra days, maybe it means many days, even earlier than the 11th.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it means many times!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back from the other side. If the word adds days, why stop at the 11th of אדר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the worry is that the word teaches too much. A plural has no clear number, so it might allow reading on the 10th, the 9th, and even earlier days.

phrases.english: Say many times!
phrases.notes: Maybe the מגילה could be read even before the 11th.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit of the derivation in step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ״זְמַנֵּיהֶם״ teaches exactly the days of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A plural has no set number, so it could include unlimited extra days

steps.title: The extra plural adds only two days
steps.stepSummary: ״זְמַנֵּיהֶם״ is compared to ״זְמַנָּם״. Just as ״זְמַנָּם״ means two days, ״זְמַנֵּיהֶם״ adds only two more.
steps.simpleTranslation: ״זְמַנֵּיהֶם״ is like ״זְמַנָּם״. Just as ״זְמַנָּם״ means two, so too ״זְמַנֵּיהֶם״ means two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the number of extra days. The longer word is read the same way as the shorter word, so it adds two days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״זְמַנָּם″ stands for two days: the 14th and the 15th. The extra plural ending works the same way, so it adds two more days and no more than that.

phrases.english: "Their times" is like "their time":
just as "their time" means two
so too "their times" means two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural could add an unlimited number of days
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra plural adds exactly two days, like ״זְמַנָּם″

steps.title: Maybe the two extra days are the 12th and 13th
steps.stepSummary: If only two days are added, maybe they are the 12th and the 13th, which would leave no source for the 11th.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then say the two days are the 12th and the 13th!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which two days were added. The closest days to פורים are the 12th and the 13th, so there would be no source for reading on the 11th.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two added days, counted back from the 14th, would naturally be the 13th and the 12th. But the משנה allows reading on the 11th too, so the count looks one day short.

phrases.english: But say the twelfth and the thirteenth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges which two days step 20 adds
steps.kashyaTarget: Including the 11th of אדר among the reading days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two closest extra days are the 12th and 13th, so there is no source for the 11th

steps.title: The 13th is already included, so the extra days are the 11th and 12th
steps.stepSummary: Based on רב שמואל בר יצחק, the 13th was the day everyone gathered to fight. It is already a fitting day, so the two extra days are the 11th and the 12th.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב שמואל בר יצחק said: the 13th is a time of gathering for everyone, so there is no need to include it. Here too: the 13th is a time of gathering for everyone, so there is no need to include it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by using a rule from רב שמואל בר יצחק. The 13th does not need the פסוק, so the two extra days must be the 11th and the 12th.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the 13th of אדר all the Jews gathered to fight their enemies, and the miracle happened then. So the 13th is naturally fit for reading and does not use up a spot. The two added days are therefore the 12th and the 11th, which fits the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: the אמורא whose rule is quoted
a time of gathering (the day the Jews gathered to fight)

steps.whatToRemember: ״זְמַנֵּיהֶם″ adds exactly two days. The 13th needs no source because it was the day of gathering for everyone. So the extra days before פורים are the 11th and the 12th. The next step asks whether they might instead come after פורים.
steps.confusionAlert: The two added days are NOT the 12th and 13th. The 13th is already fitting on its own, so the פסוק adds the 11th and the 12th.

phrases.english: As Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר זְמַן קְהִילָּה לַכֹּל הִיא,
phrases.english: the thirteenth is a time of gathering for all,
phrases.notes: The day the Jews gathered to fight their enemies.

phrases.english: and there is no need to include it;
here too:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר זְמַן קְהִילָּה לַכֹּל הִיא,
phrases.english: the thirteenth is a time of gathering for all,
and there is no need to include it.
phrases.notes: So the two added days are the 12th and the 11th.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 and completes the source for all the reading days
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying an outside rule: the 13th needs no special source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two added days are the 12th and the 13th
steps.terutzMaskana: The 13th is fitting on its own, so the added days are the 11th and the 12th

steps.title: Maybe the extra days are the 16th and 17th
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the two extra days may come after פורים, on the 16th and 17th, instead of before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say the two extra days are the 16th and the 17th!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב שמן בר אבא's derivation again. Maybe the two added days fall after פורים instead of before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 showed why the extra days should not be the 12th and 13th. The word ״זְמַנֵּיהֶם״ itself still does not say whether the days come before or after פורים. So the גמרא suggests the two days right after פורים, the 16th and the 17th.

phrases.english: But say the sixteenth and seventeenth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that the 13th is excluded and proposes the days after פורים instead.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the two extra days from ״זְמַנֵּיהֶם״ are the 11th and 12th.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word does not say which direction the extra days go, so they could be the days after Purim.

steps.title: פורים may not be pushed later
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק ״וְלֹא יַעֲבוֹר״ teaches that פורים may not be moved past its time. So the extra days cannot be the 16th and 17th.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written, "And it shall not pass."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק showing that פורים may not be moved later, so the extra days must come before פורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״וְלֹא יַעֲבוֹר״ means the reading may not pass beyond its set time. Moving it later is ruled out. Only earlier days remain, so the extra days are the 11th and 12th.

keyTerms.meaning: "And it shall not pass" (אסתר ט:כז): פורים may not be delayed

steps.whatToRemember: Extra מגילה days can only be earlier than פורים, never later, because of ״וְלֹא יַעֲבוֹר״.

phrases.english: "And it shall not pass" is written.
phrases.notes: אסתר ט:כז. פורים may not be pushed past its time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק blocks the suggested reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra days could be after פורים (16th and 17th).
steps.terutzMaskana: ״וְלֹא יַעֲבוֹר״ forbids delay, so the extra days are the 11th and 12th.

steps.title: A second source from the word ״כַּיָּמִים״
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני learns the extra days from ״כַּיָּמִים״. ״יָמִים״ means two days, and the added כ adds two more: the 11th and 12th.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: The פסוק says, "As the days on which the Jews rested." "Days" alone would be enough. "As the days" comes to include the 11th and the 12th.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different אמורא with a new source for the early reading days. This is a second approach, separate from רב שמן בר אבא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plain ״יָמִים״ (days) refers to the two main days, the 14th and 15th. The extra letter כ ("as") adds two more days, just as ״זְמַנֵּיהֶם״ did for רב שמן בר אבא. The extra days are named as the 11th and 12th.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives a second source for the extra days
"As the days". The extra כ adds more days
To include (add something not stated directly)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said,
the verse says:
"As the days on which the Jews rested."
"Days" would be enough, yet it says "as the days":
to include the eleventh and the twelfth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel source in place of רב שמן בר אבא's ״בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם״.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra כ in ״כַּיָּמִים״ adds the 11th and 12th of אדר as valid reading days.

steps.title: Maybe the extra days are the 12th and 13th
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the extra days should not be the 12th and 13th, the days right before פורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say the 12th and the 13th!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tests רבי שמואל בר נחמני's source with the same question it asked earlier. Maybe the two added days are the ones closest to פורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״כַּיָּמִים״ adds only two days, the natural choice would be the two days right before the 14th. That would leave no source for the 11th.

phrases.english: But say the twelfth and thirteenth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the new source in step 25, matching step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמואל בר נחמני's claim that the extra days are the 11th and 12th.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The closest days to פורים seem more natural, which would leave the 11th without a source.

steps.title: The 13th needs no extra source
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יצחק answers that the 13th was a day when everyone gathered. It is already a fitting day, so the added days are the 11th and 12th.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר יצחק said: The 13th is a time of gathering for everyone, and it does not need to be included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer it gave in step 22, now applied to רבי שמואל בר נחמני's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 13th is already a fitting day because the Jews gathered to fight on it. Using an extra word to add it would be wasted. So the two extra days must be the 11th and 12th.

keyTerms.meaning: A time of gathering (the Jews gathered to fight on the 13th)
There is no need to include it

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yitzḥak said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר זְמַן קְהִילָּה לַכֹּל הִיא,
phrases.english: the thirteenth is a time of gathering for all,
and it does not need to be included.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יִצְחָק: שְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר זְמַן קְהִילָּה לַכֹּל הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The 13th is already a fitting day without any extra word.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra days are the 12th and 13th.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 13th needs no source, so the extra days are the 11th and 12th.

steps.title: Maybe the days come after Purim here too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again suggests the 16th and 17th, this time against רבי שמואל בר נחמני's source.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say the 16th and the 17th!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the earlier challenge. This time it is aimed at the ״כַּיָּמִים״ source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the 13th is excluded, ״כַּיָּמִים״ could still point to days after פורים. The repetition shows that the second source faces the same test as the first.

phrases.english: But say the sixteenth and seventeenth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues testing the ״כַּיָּמִים״ source, matching step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 11th and 12th as the days added by ״כַּיָּמִים״.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The days after Purim could also be the ones added.

steps.title: ״וְלֹא יַעֲבוֹר״ rules out later days
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק blocks delaying פורים, so the ״כַּיָּמִים״ source also gives the 11th and 12th.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written, "And it shall not pass."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as in step 24: פורים may not be pushed later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״וְלֹא יַעֲבוֹר״ applies no matter which source is used. So both רב שמן בר אבא and רבי שמואל בר נחמני end up with the 11th and 12th.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sources (״בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם״ and ״כַּיָּמִים״) reach the same result: the 11th and 12th are added, the 13th needs no source, and later days are forbidden.

phrases.english: "And it shall not pass" is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The same פסוק blocks the suggested reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra days could be the 16th and 17th.
steps.terutzMaskana: פורים may not be delayed, so the extra days are the 11th and 12th.

steps.title: Why not learn it from ״בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם״?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי שמואל בר נחמני did not use רב שמן בר אבא's source, ״בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did רבי שמואל בר נחמני not learn it from "in their times"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי שמואל בר נחמני needed a different source when ״בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם״ was already available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two אמוראים give different sources for the same law, the גמרא often asks why one did not accept the other's source. This question looks for what רבי שמואל בר נחמני sees differently in ״בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם״.

keyTerms.meaning: "In their times": רב שמן בר אבא's source word

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי מַאי טַעְמָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani, what is the reason
that he did not learn it from "in their times"?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר מִבִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two sources after both have been tested.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי שמואל בר נחמני rejects ״בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם״ as a source.

steps.title: He learns nothing from the different forms of זמן
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני does not learn anything from the difference between זמן, זמנם, and זמניהם. To him, ״בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם״ only shows the two main days.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Time," "their time," "their times": he does not learn anything from these differences.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמואל בר נחמני does not see any extra meaning in the longer plural form.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שמן בר אבא learned extra days from ״זְמַנֵּיהֶם״ being longer than ״זְמַנָּם״. רבי שמואל בר נחמני treats these forms as normal ways of speaking. So for him ״בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם״ teaches only that there are two days, and he needs ״כַּיָּמִים״ to add the early days.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not learn anything from it

steps.whatToRemember: The two אמוראים disagree about whether the longer plural ״זְמַנֵּיהֶם״ teaches anything. That is why רבי שמואל בר נחמני uses ״כַּיָּמִים״ instead.

phrases.english: "Time," "their time," "their times":
he does not learn anything from these.

steps.triggerLanguage: זְמַן זְמַנָּם זְמַנֵּיהֶם לָא מַשְׁמַע לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמואל בר נחמני does not learn from the different forms of the word זמן, so ״בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם״ gives him only two days.

steps.title: Why didn't רב שמן בר אבא use ״כַּיָּמִים״?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the reverse question: why didn't רב שמן בר אבא learn the extra days from ״כַּיָּמִים״, like רבי שמואל בר נחמני did?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב שמן בר אבא, why didn't he learn it from ״כַּיָּמִים״?
steps.whatsHappening: Step 30 asked why רבי שמואל בר נחמני did not use רב שמן בר אבא's source. Now the גמרא asks the opposite question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each אמורא has a different פסוק for the extra reading days. The גמרא wants to know why רב שמן בר אבא skipped the source of ״כַּיָּמִים״. The answer will show that he needs that פסוק for something else.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As the days' — a word in the מגילה, used by רבי שמואל בר נחמני as his source

phrases.english: And Rav Shemen bar Abba —
what is the reason he did not say it from 'as the days'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror question to Step 30
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב שמן בר אבא does not use ״כַּיָּמִים״ as the source for the extra days

steps.title: 'As the days' is about future generations
steps.stepSummary: רב שמן בר אבא says ״כַּיָּמִים״ is needed for a different lesson: פורים is kept on these days for all generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would say to you: that פסוק is written about the generations to come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב שמן בר אבא reads ״כַּיָּמִים״ as teaching something else, so he cannot use it for the extra days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To רב שמן בר אבא, ״כַּיָּמִים״ means: just as the Jews rested on these days then, they will celebrate on these days in every generation. Since the word is already used for that lesson, it is not free to teach early reading days. So he uses ״בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם״ instead.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you (the גמרא explains his reasoning)
For the generations — for all future times

steps.whatToRemember: Both sources are explained: רבי שמואל בר נחמני learns nothing from זמן/זמנם/זמניהם, and רב שמן בר אבא needs ״כַּיָּמִים״ for the lesson about future generations.

phrases.english: He would say to you:
That verse is written about future generations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 32
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״כַּיָּמִים״ is needed for the lesson that פורים is kept on these days in every generation

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא; the חכמים allow only the 14th
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says our משנה is the view of רבי עקיבא, who learns from זמן/זמנם/זמניהם. The חכמים say the מגילה is read only on its fixed day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This is the view of רבי עקיבא, the source of unnamed teachings, who learns from ״זְמַן״, ״זְמַנָּם״, ״זְמַנֵּיהֶם״. But the חכמים say: we read it only in its time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. רבי יוחנן states whose opinion the משנה follows when it allows villagers to read early on the day of gathering, and he says the חכמים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says the early reading days depend on רבי עקיבא's way of learning from small changes in wording. The חכמים do not learn this way, so they allow reading only on the 14th. This means the משנה is not a view everyone agrees with.

keyTerms.meaning: The unnamed one — רבי עקיבא, whose views stand behind many unnamed משניות
He expounds — he learns a law from the wording
In its fixed time (the 14th of אדר)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basis for the rest of the סוגיא: if only רבי עקיבא allows early reading, we must ask whether the halacha follows him.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
This is the statement of Rabbi Akiva, the unattributed one,
who expounds 'time,' 'their time,' 'their times.'
But the Sages say:
One reads it only in its designated time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New branch after the source discussion closed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא; the חכמים allow reading only on the 14th

steps.title: רבי יהודה: early reading only applied in earlier times
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says early reading was allowed only when the calendar was fixed properly and the Jews lived in their land. Nowadays we read only on the fixed day.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: רבי יהודה said: When does this apply? When the years are set properly and the Jews live in their land. But nowadays, since people look to it for counting, we read it only in its time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רבי יוחנן. This step quotes the source; the next steps work out exactly how it challenges him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says the early days are canceled only 'nowadays'. That suggests that in earlier times, everyone allowed early reading, not just רבי עקיבא. That goes against רבי יוחנן, who said the חכמים always allow only the 14th.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא)
Set properly (the calendar is fixed correctly)
They look to it — people use פורים to count to פסח

steps.confusionAlert: 'Looking to it' means people use the day of פורים to know when פסח falls, one month later. If villagers read early, they could count wrongly.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Rabbi Yehuda said:
When does this apply?
At a time when the years are set properly
and the Jewish people dwell in their land.
But nowadays,
since people look to it,
one reads it only in its designated time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's statement in Step 34
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the חכמים allow reading only on the 14th
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה limits the ban to 'nowadays', which suggests that in earlier times early reading was allowed by all

steps.title: Whose view does רבי יהודה follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which opinion רבי יהודה's ruling is based on.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה — according to whom is he speaking?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins working out the challenge. It asks whose opinion רבי יהודה follows, and will test each choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To know whether the ברייתא really challenges רבי יוחנן, the גמרא must know which opinion רבי יהודה is explaining. If he explains the חכמים, then the חכמים once allowed early reading.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda — in accordance with whose opinion?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא from Step 35
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view רבי יהודה is explaining

steps.title: It cannot follow רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי יהודה cannot be following רבי עקיבא, because for רבי עקיבא early reading applies even nowadays.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he follows רבי עקיבא — but even nowadays this rule applies!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first choice and rejects it. This prepares for the next option: that רבי יהודה follows the חכמים, which would challenge רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא learns the early days from the פסוק, and he never limits them to earlier times. So רבי יהודה, who cancels early reading nowadays, cannot be following רבי עקיבא. This leaves the חכמים as the likely choice.

keyTerms.meaning: The ordinance (the rule allowing early reading)

phrases.english: If we say it is according to Rabbi Akiva —
even nowadays
this ordinance applies!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first answer to Step 36
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that רבי יהודה follows רבי עקיבא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי עקיבא allows early reading even nowadays, but רבי יהודה does not

steps.title: רבי יהודה must follow the חכמים, who allowed early reading in good times
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יהודה cannot follow רבי עקיבא, he must follow the חכמים. Yet his ruling allows early reading when the calendar is fixed and the Jews live in their land. This shows that the חכמים themselves allowed early reading back then, which contradicts רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not according to the חכמים? And at least when the years are set properly and the Jews live in their land, we do read early.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge against רבי יוחנן. The ברייתא of רבי יהודה must follow the חכמים, and it still allows early reading in the old days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 37 ruled out רבי עקיבא, so the only option left is the חכמים. רבי יהודה forbids early reading only nowadays, which means that in better times even the חכמים allowed it. But רבי יוחנן said the חכמים allow reading only on the fixed day, with no exception.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that… (introduces the only remaining option)
According to the view of the Sages
In their proper order (the calendar is set correctly)

phrases.english: Rather, is it not according to the Sages?
phrases.notes: The only option left after Step 37 rejected רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: And at a time when the years are set properly
phrases.notes: The calendar is fixed correctly by the בית דין.

phrases.english: and the Jews dwell in their land —
at least then we do read (early),

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the process of elimination begun in Steps 36-37 and turns it against רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim (Step 34) that the חכמים allow reading the מגילה only on its fixed day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה must follow the חכמים, and he allows early reading in good times. So the חכמים do allow early reading at least sometimes, which contradicts רבי יוחנן's absolute statement.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי יוחנן's statement is conclusively refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The refutation of רבי יוחנן is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא declares that the challenge stands and that רבי יוחנן's statement is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is offered to defend רבי יוחנן. The repeated word תיובתא shows that the refutation is final, at least according to this first version of his statement.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation; the opinion is rejected

phrases.english: The refutation of Rabbi Yochanan is a refutation.

steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, רבי יוחנן said the חכמים never allow early reading. The ברייתא of רבי יהודה disproves this.
steps.confusionAlert: Only this version of רבי יוחנן's statement is refuted. The very next step brings a different version that survives.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Seals the challenge of Step 38 as unanswerable.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first version of רבי יוחנן's statement is rejected: the חכמים did allow early reading in times when the calendar was fixed and the Jews lived in their land.

steps.title: A second version of רבי יוחנן's statement
steps.stepSummary: Some report רבי יוחנן's statement differently. Our משנה is the view of רבי עקיבא, but the חכמים forbid early reading only nowadays, because people look at the מגילה reading to count toward פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This is the view of רבי עקיבא, the unnamed author. But the חכמים said: nowadays, since people look to it, we read it only in its proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another version of רבי יוחנן's statement. In this version, the חכמים limit the ban on early reading to our times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the חכמים do not forbid early reading completely. They forbid it only nowadays, because people use the date of the מגילה reading to figure out when פסח falls. Since this version admits that early reading was once allowed, it does not clash with רבי יהודה's ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say (an alternate version)
The unnamed one; the author behind an anonymous ruling
People look to it, using the reading to calculate when פסח falls

phrases.english: There are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbah bar bar Chanah said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
This is the view of Rabbi Akiva, the unnamed author,
phrases.notes: Our משנה, which doesn't name its author, follows רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: but the Sages said: nowadays,
since people look to it —
phrases.notes: People count from פורים to know when פסח comes, so an early reading could confuse that count.

phrases.english: we read it only in its proper time.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. Version 1: the חכמים always require the fixed day. Version 2: the חכמים require the fixed day only nowadays.
steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of רבי יוחנן's statement, one that avoids the refutation of Step 39.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה follows רבי עקיבא. According to the חכמים, nowadays the מגילה is read only on its fixed day, because people use the reading to calculate פסח.

steps.title: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה supports the second version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יהודה's ברייתא matches the second version. Early reading was allowed in good times, but nowadays the מגילה is read only on its fixed day, for the same reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה said: When does this apply? When the years are set properly and the Jews dwell in their land. But nowadays, since people look to it, we read it only in its proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא of רבי יהודה again, this time as support for the second version of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same ברייתא that refuted the first version now fits perfectly with the second. Both say early reading was allowed in the past and is forbidden nowadays. Both also give the same reason: people look to the reading.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא (introduces supporting proof)

phrases.english: It is also taught this way (in a baraita):
Rabbi Yehuda said: When (is early reading allowed)?
At a time when the years are set properly
and the Jews dwell in their land,
but nowadays,
since people look to it —
we read it only in its proper time.

steps.whatToRemember: According to the second version, the חכמים and רבי יהודה agree: early reading was allowed in the past, but nowadays we read only on the fixed day.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why, in practice, we do not read the מגילה early today.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second version of רבי יוחנן (Step 40) with the ברייתא first brought in Step 35.
steps.raayaObject: The second version of רבי יוחנן: the חכמים forbid early reading only nowadays.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יהודה, which allows early reading only when the calendar is fixed and the Jews live in their land, and gives the reason that people look to the reading.

steps.title: רב אשי raises a contradiction between two rulings of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי finds a difficulty between רבי יהודה in this ברייתא and רבי יהודה elsewhere, in a משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי had a difficulty: רבי יהודה contradicts רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. רב אשי announces that two rulings of רבי יהודה seem to contradict each other, and the details come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that nowadays the מגילה is never read early. Another source, a משנה quoting רבי יהודה, seems to say something different about early reading. The next lines will quote it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was difficult for him; he had a question
A contradiction between one statement of רבי יהודה and another statement of his

phrases.english: Rav Ashi had a difficulty:
(a ruling of) Rabbi Yehuda against (another ruling of) Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: The second source, a משנה, is quoted on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ברייתא of רבי יהודה from Step 41 and opens a new question about whether his rulings are consistent.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רבי יהודה's view in the ברייתא (no early reading nowadays).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ruling in רבי יהודה's name, in a משנה, appears to conflict with the ברייתא. The full contradiction is spelled out in the next lines.
